title: Local descent of continuous scalar cochain boundaries from the norm completion
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Let $\iota:\Omega\hookrightarrow\widehat\Omega$ be the isometric field embedding into its metric completion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Let $G$ be any profinite group (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group), and let $S$ be any profinite set in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For $F=\Omega,\widehat\Omega$ put $C_F^r(S,G)=C(S\times G^r,F)$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], with trivial $G$-action on coefficients, $C_F^0(S,G)=C(S,F)$, $d^0=0$, and
$$(df)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=f(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{j=1}^{r}(-1)^j f(s;g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}f(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
For every integer $n\geq1$, suppose $z\in C_\Omega^n(S,G)$ satisfies $dz=0$ and there exists $b\in C_{\widehat\Omega}^{n-1}(S,G)$ with $db=\iota\circ z$. Then there is a finite family of continuous maps $u_a:S_a\to S$ of profinite sets whose images jointly cover $S$, and there are $b_a\in C_\Omega^{n-1}(S_a,G)$ such that
$$d b_a=z\circ(u_a\times1_{G^n}).$$
For $S=\varnothing$ the empty covering family is allowed. Equalities are equalities of actual cochains, with no closure of coboundaries. This assertion assumes existence of a completed primitive; it asserts no vanishing of cohomology for $G$ and no comparison with internal right derived invariants.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, use the empty family. If $n=1$, then $db=d^0b=0$; the embedding $\iota$ is injective, so $z=0$, and the zero degree-zero cochain is already a primitive. Henceforth $S\ne\varnothing$ and $n\geq2$. We construct a primitive on $S$ itself; the required cover will be the single identity map. Identify $\Omega$ with its isometric image in $B=\widehat\Omega$ using [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. The strong triangle inequality holds in $\Omega$: any two algebraic elements lie in one finite extension, where [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] applies. It holds in $B$ by passage to limits, as does scalar norm homogeneity over $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Boundary cases and norm topologies.

proof.text:
Read the profinite set $S$ as a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space; it has a basis of clopen sets by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis]. By [lem-sfb-profinite-group-open-normal-subgroup-basis], the original compact Hausdorff totally disconnected group $G$ has a neighbourhood basis of open normal subgroups. Thus $S$ and $G$ satisfy the hypotheses of the next input. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-metric-function-quotients], with $r=n$ and the product metric target $\Omega\times B$, to
$$F(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n)=(z(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n),b(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})).$$
It gives continuous surjections $p:S\to S_0$, $q:G\to G_0$, the latter a homomorphism, with $S_0,G_0$ metrizable profinite. The first component descends $z$; evaluating the last group argument at $1$ in the second component descends $b$. Its independence of that argument follows by surjectivity of $p,q$. Surjectivity on all powers shows $dz_0=0$ and $db_0=\iota z_0$. A primitive on these quotients pulls back to the original spaces. Rename them $S,G,z,b$ in the rest of the proof.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Simultaneous metrizable reduction of the cocycle and its given primitive.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and choose increasing closed finite fields $F_N$ covering $\Omega$. Set
$$f(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)=z(s;g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n).$$
For each $s$, the closed sets $f(s,-)^{-1}(F_N)$ cover the nonempty compact Hausdorff $G^{n+1}$. By [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior] one has nonempty interior. A product neighbourhood in that interior contains $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$ for some open normal subgroup $H$: intersect finitely many translated neighbourhoods of $1$ and apply [lem-sfb-profinite-group-open-normal-subgroup-basis]. Thus every $s$ has a certificate consisting of such a rectangle and a field $F_N$. No neighbourhood of $s$ is asserted to have that certificate.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Countably many closed certificate sets; Stacks Tag 0CQN, lemma-baire-category-locally-compact.

proof.text:
A compact metric profinite space has a countable clopen basis: for each positive integer $t$, choose clopen neighbourhoods of diameter $<2^{-t}$ and take a finite subcover. The union of these finite covers is a basis. Every clopen subset is a finite union of basis members, by compactness. Apply this to $G$: there are countably many open subgroups and their cosets, hence countably many coset rectangles. Enumerate all rectangle/field pairs with nonempty certificate sets as $(B_j,N_j)$, $j\geq1$, repeating entries if the list is finite, and put
$$A_j=\{s:f(s,B_j)\subseteq F_{N_j}\}.$$
Each $A_j$ is closed, as an intersection of inverse images of the closed field $F_{N_j}$ under continuous evaluation maps. The preceding step gives $S=\bigcup_{j\geq1}A_j$, with every $A_j$ nonempty. Write $B_j=H_ja_{j,0}\times\cdots\times H_ja_{j,n}$. Each $H_j$ has finite index: its disjoint open cosets cover compact $G$, hence admit a finite subcover.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Countability from compactness and clopen bases.

proof.text: Choose finite clopen partitions $\mathcal P_t$ of $S$ refining each other, with all atom diameters $<2^{-t}$. Obtain them from finite clopen covers at each scale by taking their finite Boolean refinements and then common refinements. Map $S$ to $D=\prod_t\mathcal P_t$ by its atom at each level. This map $e$ is continuous. It is injective because the mesh tends to zero; its inverse on its image is continuous because fixing the $t$th coordinate confines the inverse to one atom of diameter $<2^{-t}$. For each $j$, $e(A_j)$ is compact and closed in the Hausdorff space $D$: a point outside this compact set has neighbourhoods separating it from each of its points, and finitely many of the latter neighbourhoods cover the set. Apply [lem-sfb-countable-discrete-product-closed-retraction] to the nonempty closed subset $e(A_j)\subseteq D$. Restrict the resulting map to $e(S)$ and compose with $e^{-1}$. This gives a continuous $\rho_j:S\to A_j$ fixing $A_j$ pointwise.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Closed-parameter retractions using the exact Mathlib product theorem.

proof.text: For $i\geq1$ let $U_{j,i}$ be the union of the atoms of $\mathcal P_i$ meeting $A_j$. These are clopen, decrease with $i$, and have intersection $A_j$: a point outside the closed $A_j$ has positive distance from it and is eventually in an atom disjoint from it. Let $k_i(s)$ be the least $j\leq i$ with $s\in U_{j,i}$, or $1$ when none exists. This is locally constant with finite range. For each $s$, let $j(s)$ be the least $j$ with $s\in A_j$. Eventually all $j<j(s)$ are excluded from $U_{j,i}$, while $s\in U_{j(s),i}$ always. Thus $k_i(s)=j(s)$ for all sufficiently large $i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. A continuous finite-choice approximation with pointwise eventual stabilization.

proof.text: For each rectangle $B_j$ choose the operator $T_j$ of [lem-sfb-finite-index-rectangle-primitive-operator], with $C_j=|[G:H_j]|_\ell^{-1}$. It works for every coefficient field used below and for profinite parameter families. In particular, for every cocycle $c$ with homogeneous function zero on $B_j$, one has $dT_jc=c$. All $C_j$ are finite, even when the subgroup index is divisible by $\ell$. Put $D_t=\max(1,C_1,\ldots,C_t)$ for $t\geq1$ and $\delta_i=2^{-i}/D_{i+1}$ for $i\geq0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Rectangle primitives with arbitrary finite-index norm loss.

proof.text: For every $N$, [lem-sfb-norm-one-finite-subfield-projection] gives a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear contraction $p_N:\Omega\to F_N$ fixing $F_N$. The finite field $F_N$ is complete by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] to the dense normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-subspace $\Omega\subseteq B$, with target $F_N$. It extends $p_N$ to a linear contraction $P_N:B\to F_N$, still fixing $F_N$. Density here is the defining density of the canonical inclusion in the metric completion; no continuous retraction $B\to\Omega$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Extend only the finite-field projections, whose targets are complete.

proof.text:
For each $i\geq0$, compactness of the images of $z$ and $b$ gives finite $\delta_i$-nets with centres in $\Omega$ (use its density in $B$ for the image of $b$). Choose strictly increasing $L_i\geq i$ so that $F_{L_i}$ contains all these centres and $L_i\geq N_j$ for $j\leq i+1$. This is possible since the increasing $F_N$ cover $\Omega$. Put $P_i=P_{L_i}$. If $a\in F_{L_i}$ is a chosen centre within $\delta_i$ of $x$, contractivity and $P_ia=a$ give
$$|P_ix-x|\leq\max(|P_i(x-a)|,|a-x|)\leq\delta_i.$$
Consequently $\|P_iz-z\|_\infty\leq\delta_i$ and $\|P_ib-b\|_\infty\leq\delta_i$. The same choice controls both maps and all the first $i+1$ rectangle constants.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Accelerate the field filtration to absorb unbounded subgroup indices.

proof.text: Set $P_{-1}=0$, $e_i=(P_i-P_{i-1})z$ and $c_i=(P_i-P_{i-1})b$ for $i\geq0$. All are continuous $F_{L_i}$-valued cochains; the linear coefficient maps commute with every finite sum in $d$, so $dc_i=e_i$ and $de_i=0$. Their telescoping sums are $\sum_{h=0}^ie_h=P_iz\to z$. For $i\geq1$, both supremum norms are at most $\max(\delta_i,\delta_{i-1})$. At any fixed input $(s,y)$ of $z$, $e_i(s,y)$ is eventually zero: the algebraic value $z(s,y)$ lies in one $F_N$ and both projections eventually fix it. This last assertion is made only for $z$, not for the completed primitive $b$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Finite-field cochains with small norms and pointwise finite cocycle differences.

proof.text:
For $i\geq1$ and $j\leq i$ put $v_{i,j}=c_i-T_je_i$ and define
$$B_{i,j}(s,x)=(T_je_i)(s,x)+v_{i,j}(s,x)-v_{i,j}(\rho_j(s),x).$$
These are continuous $F_{L_i}$-valued cochains. At $a\in A_j$, the homogeneous values of $z(a,-)$ on $B_j$ lie in $F_{N_j}$, which both $P_i$ and $P_{i-1}$ fix since $L_{i-1}\geq N_j$. Thus the homogeneous function of $e_i(a,-)$ vanishes there. The rectangle operator gives $dT_je_i(a,-)=e_i(a,-)$, so $dv_{i,j}(a,-)=0$. Therefore
$$dB_{i,j}=dT_je_i+(e_i-dT_je_i)-0=e_i.$$
Also $B_{i,j}(s,-)=T_je_i(s,-)$ for $s\in A_j$, because $\rho_j(s)=s$. Its supremum norm is at most $\max(\|c_i\|_\infty,C_j\|e_i\|_\infty)$, by the ultrametric inequality and the operator bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Subtract a retracted cocycle to force agreement on the closed certificate set.

proof.text:
Let $b_0=c_0$. For $i\geq1$ define $b_i(s,x)=B_{i,k_i(s)}(s,x)$. The finitely many clopen pieces of $k_i$ make this a continuous $F_{L_i}$-valued cochain with $db_i=e_i$. Since $k_i(s)\leq i$, the preceding bound and $D_i\max(\delta_i,\delta_{i-1})\leq2^{-(i-1)}$ give $\|b_i\|_\infty\leq2^{-(i-1)}$. Here $D_i\delta_{i-1}=2^{-(i-1)}$ and $D_i\delta_i\leq2^{-i}$. Fix $(s,x)$. Eventually $k_i(s)=j(s)$ and $s\in A_{j(s)}$, so
$$b_i(s,x)=T_{j(s)}e_i(s,x)=\sum_{a=1}^{u_{j(s)}}\alpha_{j(s),a}e_i(s,\psi_{j(s),a}(x)).$$
This is one fixed finite list of evaluations. Each term is eventually zero by step 10. Hence $b_i(s,x)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of coefficient-completion boundary descent. Clopen assembly, uniform smallness and the separate pointwise-finiteness argument.

proof.text:
The partial sums $\sum_{i=0}^Nb_i$ are uniformly Cauchy into the complete field $B$: by the ultrametric inequality every tail has norm at most the largest norm of its terms, and those norms tend to zero. Their pointwise limits therefore give a uniform limit $b_*:S\times G^{n-1}\to B$. For continuity, approximate $b_*$ uniformly within any prescribed positive error by one continuous partial sum and use the strong triangle inequality near the point in question. Step 12 makes every value a finite sum in $\Omega$; the isometric subspace topology then makes $b_*$ continuous into $\Omega$ itself. At a fixed input $d$ is a finite sum of evaluations, so
$$db_*=\lim_Nd\Big(\sum_{i=0}^Nb_i\Big)=\lim_NP_Nz=z.$$
Pull back this cochain by $p\times q^{n-1}$ from step 2. It is a genuine $\Omega$-valued continuous primitive on the original $S$. Choose $S_1=S$, $u_1=\mathrm{id}_S$. This proves the requested assertion with actual equality of cochains.
